note: What a server sends to say something happened that the whole match is told about. What sort of thing is named first, and the sort settles what follows. The header names no object: it carries zero.

fields.name: event
fields.note: Which event, from 0 to 144, and so which fields follow.

fields.name: source
fields.note: The unit the thing is credited to, or zero where none is.

fields.name: subject
fields.note: The unit the thing happened to, or zero where none is named.

fields.name: stage
fields.note: A client reads it and shows nothing for it; a server writes zero.

fields.name: damage

fields.name: physical

fields.name: magical
fields.note: Magical damage.

fields.name: true
fields.note: True damage.

fields.name: sourceKind
fields.note: What sort of source it was.

fields.name: script
fields.note: The spell or effect, by the number its name gives, shown by name.

fields.name: parentScript
fields.note: The spell or effect it came from, by the number its name gives, shown by name.

fields.name: parentCaster
fields.note: What it carries is not recorded for this range; a server writes zero.

fields.name: parent

bits.name: source

bits.name: side
bits.note: What it means is not recorded for this range; a server writes zero.

bits.name: category
bits.note: A client sums two entries of this sort where this, the source kinds and both spells match, and, where this is zero, the subjects match too.

bits.name: spellLevel
bits.note: The rank of the spell, as shown.

fields.name: spent

fields.name: critical

fields.name: spree

fields.name: side

32.name: inhibitorDied
32.note: Sent as an inhibitor falls, with that inhibitor as source and the unit credited with it as subject. A client calls out the kill, naming the killer, the inhibitor and the assisters, where it holds the inhibitor as a building and knows the killer. Where it names the client's own champion and everything after it is zero, a client on map 1 shows a notice with no text of its own.

70.name: playerLeft
70.note: Sent as a player's client leaves the match, naming that player's champion as subject. A client announces that a player has quit; where the seat's name is unknown, a client names an unknown player.
